title: Synaptic dysfunction as a major driver in Alzheimer's disease: Beyond the amyloid paradigm
title_zh: 突触功能障碍作为阿尔茨海默病主要驱动因素：超越淀粉样范式
abstract: While β-amyloid (Aβ) peptides have dominated Alzheimer's disease (AD) research for decades, the unexpected failure of several anti-amyloid therapies has underscored critical gaps in our understanding of the early pathogenic mechanisms of AD. This review presents a fundamental re-evaluation of the causal chain in AD pathogenesis: the previously dominant amyloid-centric model may need to be shifted toward synaptic dysfunction coupled with glutamate excitotoxicity and neurometabolic failure as potential major drivers of cognitive decline in AD. We gather emerging evidence demonstrating that neuronal hyperactivity and glutamate excitotoxicity-both potentially independent of amyloid deposition-can contribute to synaptic damage at preclinical stages of AD. We propose that the chronic neuronal burden of metabolic overload, rather than amyloid toxicity alone, may trigger a cascade of synaptic deterioration and neuronal death. This metabolic-energetic framework introduces a new biological economy to neurodegeneration, in which neurons are compromised by unbalanced energy demands that are only later amplified by protein toxicity. By integrating recent findings on glutamate dysregulation with amyloid and tau pathology, we present a multifactorial model that emphasizes the temporal primacy and mechanistic interplay of excitotoxicity in early synaptic dysfunction, rather than treating these pathways as parallel or independent events. This model offers an explanation for why amyloid removal so often fails: intervening at the level of downstream synaptic damage is likely too late. This reframing carries profound therapeutic implications: targeting synaptic health and glutamate homeostasis before the onset of irreversible amyloid-driven damage may yield more effective preventive strategies than current approaches that predominantly focus on amyloid removal. This synapse-focused perspective prioritizes synaptic health and repositions amyloid as one contributing factor within a broader, integrated model of AD.
abstract_zh: 尽管β-淀粉样蛋白（Aβ）肽几十年来主导了AD研究，但多项抗Aβ治疗的意外失败突显了我们对AD早期致病机制理解中的关键缺口。该综述对AD发病的因果链进行了根本性再评估：此前占主导地位的淀粉样中心模型可能需要转向突触功能障碍，并与谷氨酸兴奋毒性及神经代谢失败相结合，作为认知下降的潜在主要驱动。我们整合新兴证据，显示神经元过度活动和谷氨酸兴奋毒性——二者均可能独立于淀粉样蛋白沉积——可在AD临床前阶段引发突触损伤。我们提出，慢性神经元所承受的代谢超负荷，而非仅仅是淀粉样毒性，可能触发突触恶化和神经元死亡的级联。该代谢—能量框架为神经退行性改变引入了新的生物学经济学：神经元受到失衡能量需求的损害，后期再被蛋白质毒性进一步放大。通过将近期关于谷氨酸失调与淀粉样、tau病理的发现整合，我们提出一个多因素模型，强调早期突触功能障碍中兴奋毒性的时间优先性与机制交互，而非将其视为并行或独立事件。该模型解释了为何清除Aβ常常失败：在下游突触损伤层面干预通常过晚。该重构具有深远的治疗意义：在不可逆的淀粉样驱动损伤出现前，靶向突触健康和谷氨酸稳态可能比当前主要聚焦Aβ清除的策略更有效地实现预防。该突触聚焦视角将突触健康置于优先地位，并将Aβ重新定位为更广泛整合AD模型中的一个贡献因素。
